mainTopic: The חליצה ceremony: its order, how the פסוקים are read and recorded, the rules of spitting, and who calls out 'חלוץ הנעל'
overview: The משנה describes the חליצה ceremony step by step. The judges advise the יבם, then the יבמה and the יבם each say their פסוק in לשון הקודש. She removes his shoe, spits so the judges see it, and says 'ככה יעשה לאיש.' Since רבי הורקנוס, the whole פרשה is read, and the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה argue over who calls out 'חלוץ הנעל.' In the גמרא, רב יהודה teaches that the order is the ideal way but not required, and a ברייתא backs this up. אביי and רבא argue about pausing after 'לא' when prompting the פסוקים, and רב כהנא says even רבא agrees about 'לא אבה יבמי.' The גמרא then discusses how to write a שטר חליצה, and the הלכה follows מר זוטרא, who wrote out the whole passage. It ends with rules for valid spitting and a story of רבי טרפון having everyone call out 'חלוץ הנעל' three times.

steps.title: The couple comes to court and gets advice
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens the ceremony of חליצה. The יבם and יבמה come to בית דין, and the judges give him advice that fits his situation, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: This is how חליצה is done. He and his יבמה come to בית דין, and the judges give him advice that is right for him, as the פסוק says: 'The elders of his city shall call him and speak to him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins describing how a חליצה is done. The first stage is that the couple comes to בית דין and the judges advise the יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before anything else happens, the judges talk with the יבם about what is best for him: יבום or חליצה. The משנה learns this from the פסוק 'ודברו אליו', which says the elders speak to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The ceremony that frees the יבמה, done by removing the יבם's shoe
His יבמה, his dead brother's widow
Advice that is fitting or appropriate
The elders of his city, meaning the judges

phrases.english: MISHNA
The מצוה of chalitza:
he and his yevama come to the court,
and they give him
phrases.notes: 'They' means the judges of the court.

phrases.english: advice that is fitting for him,
as it is stated:
'And the elders of his city shall call him
and speak to him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִצְוַת חֲלִיצָה: בָּא הוּא וִיבִמְתּוֹ לְבֵית דִּין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חליצה process begins with the couple coming to בית דין, where the judges give the יבם fitting advice, as learned from 'ודברו אליו'.

steps.title: She speaks, he answers, in Hebrew
steps.stepSummary: The יבמה says her פסוק saying the יבם refuses to do יבום. The יבם answers with 'I do not wish to take her.' Both are said in לשון הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: She says: 'My brother-in-law refuses to establish a name for his brother in Israel; he does not want to do יבום with me.' He says: 'I do not wish to take her.' They would say these in the holy language.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the two spoken statements of the ceremony. She speaks first, then he answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the actual פסוקים from the תורה, and they must be said in לשון הקודש, not translated. The order here, her statement before his, is what רב יהודה will later repeat in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: My brother-in-law refuses
He did not want
I do not wish to take her
The holy language, meaning Hebrew

phrases.english: And she says:
'My brother-in-law refuses to establish
a name for his brother in Israel;
he does not want to do yibum with me,'
and he says:
'I do not wish to take her.'
And they would say it in the holy language.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִיא אוֹמֶרֶת: מֵאֵן יְבָמִי לְהָקִים לְאָחִיו שֵׁם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She recites 'מאן יבמי' and he recites 'לא חפצתי לקחתה', both in לשון הקודש.

steps.title: Removing the shoe, spitting, and her final declaration
steps.stepSummary: The יבמה removes the shoe and spits in front of the judges, so the spit must be visible to them. Then she declares 'ככה יעשה לאיש.' Originally, the judges prompted the reading only up to here.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His יבמה shall approach him before the elders, remove his shoe from his foot, and spit before him.' This means spit that the judges can see. 'And she shall answer and say: So shall be done to the man who does not build his brother's house.' Up to here they would prompt them to read.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the physical acts of חליצה and the closing words she says. It ends by noting where the prompted reading used to stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From 'לעיני הזקנים' the משנה learns that the spit must be seen by the judges. The judges would read the words out for the couple to repeat, and they used to stop after 'ככה יעשה לאיש'. This sets up the next step, which tells how the custom changed.

keyTerms.meaning: And she removes his shoe
And she spits
Spit that the judges can see
They would prompt the reading, reading aloud for the couple to repeat

steps.confusionAlert: 'בפניו' here does not require spitting on his face. The משנה reads it as spit in front of him that the judges can see.

phrases.english: 'And his yevama shall approach him
before the eyes of the elders
and remove his shoe from on his foot
and spit before him,'
spit that is visible to the judges.
'And she shall answer and say:
So shall be done to the man

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִבְנֶה אֶת בֵּית אָחִיו״.
phrases.english: who does not build his brother's house.'
Up to here they would prompt the reading.
phrases.notes: The judges said the words aloud and the couple repeated after them.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: She removes the shoe and spits so the judges can see it, then says 'ככה יעשה'. The prompted reading originally ended there.

steps.title: רבי הורקנוס starts the custom of reading the whole passage
steps.stepSummary: After רבי הורקנוס once prompted the whole פרשה, it became the set custom to finish it, including the פסוק 'ונקרא שמו בישראל בית חלוץ הנעל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי הורקנוס prompted the reading under the אלה tree in כפר עיטם and finished the whole passage, it became the custom to finish the whole passage: 'And his name shall be called in Israel: the house of the one whose shoe was removed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a short story about how the custom changed. One rabbi read the whole passage, and from then on everyone did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the reading stopped at 'ככה יעשה'. רבי הורקנוס added the next פסוק, and the practice became fixed. This brings in the words 'חלוץ הנעל', which the next step discusses.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose practice set the custom
They became established, it became a set custom
The תורה passage of חליצה
The house of the one whose shoe was removed

phrases.english: And when Rabbi Hyrkanus prompted the reading
under the ela tree in the village of Eitam,
and finished the whole passage,
it became established to finish the whole passage.
'And his name shall be called in Israel:
The house of the one whose shoe was removed.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁהִקְרָא רַבִּי הוּרְקָנוֹס תַּחַת הָאֵלָה בִּכְפַר עֵיטָם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since רבי הורקנוס, the custom is to read the whole פרשה through 'בית חלוץ הנעל'.

steps.title: Who says 'חלוץ הנעל'
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says the מצוה of calling out 'חלוץ הנעל' belongs to the judges only, not the students. רבי יהודה says everyone standing there should call it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה is on the judges, not on the students. רבי יהודה says: it is a מצוה on everyone standing there to say 'חלוץ הנעל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת about who must call out 'חלוץ הנעל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'ונקרא שמו', meaning his name shall be called, but it does not say by whom. The תנא קמא limits this to the judges. רבי יהודה extends it to everyone present.

keyTerms.meaning: Judges
Students, the onlookers who are not judges
Everyone standing there
The תנא who disagrees with the תנא קמא

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's order: advice, then her statement, his statement, the shoe removal, the spit, and her final declaration. Today the whole פרשה is read. Who calls out 'חלוץ הנעל' is a מחלוקת.

phrases.english: The מצוה is on the judges,
and it is not a מצוה on the students.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
It is a מצוה on all those standing there
to say: 'The one whose shoe was removed.'

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא holds that only the judges call out 'חלוץ הנעל'. רבי יהודה holds that everyone present does.

steps.title: רב יהודה lists the order of חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה states the order: she recites, he recites, then she removes the shoe, spits, and recites.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רב יהודה said: The מצוה of חליצה is: she reads, he reads, then she removes the shoe, spits, and reads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב יהודה giving a short list of the ceremony's order. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His list matches the order in the משנה exactly. That is why the גמרא will ask what he is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the אמוראים on the משנה
The אמורא who gives the order
She reads, and he reads
She removes the shoe and spits

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Yehuda said:
The מצוה of chalitza:
she reads and he reads,
phrases.notes: She says 'מאן יבמי', then he says 'לא חפצתי לקחתה'.

phrases.english: and she removes the shoe, and spits, and reads.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, מִצְוַת חֲלִיצָה: קוֹרְאָה וְקוֹרֵא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of חליצה is: she reads, he reads, then she removes the shoe, spits, and reads.

steps.title: Isn't this already in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב יהודה adds, since the משנה already gives this exact order.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? It is the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's statement as seemingly unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא is not expected to simply repeat a משנה. So the גמרא pushes to find what new point is hidden in his words.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? What is new here?

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
It is the mishna!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's list of the order of חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His statement seems to repeat the משנה word for word, so it appears to add nothing.

steps.title: The order is ideal but not required
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה is teaching that this order is the proper way to do the מצוה, but if the order was switched, the חליצה is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he teaches us: the מצוה is done this way, but if one reversed the order, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב יהודה adds a new point: the order is only the preferred way, not a requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the משנה alone, we might think the order is required and that changing it ruins the חליצה. רב יהודה's wording 'מצות חליצה' shows the order is only the ideal (לכתחילה). After the fact, a reversed order does not make the חליצה invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he teaches us
If one reversed it
We have no problem with it

steps.whatToRemember: The order of חליצה is the ideal way (מצוה), but it is not required. If the order is switched, the חליצה is still valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This separates doing a מצוה in its best form from doing it validly at all, a distinction that comes up all over the laws of חליצה.

phrases.english: This is what he teaches us:
the מצוה is like this,
but if one reversed the order,
we have no problem with it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a new point in the wording: 'מצוה' means the ideal way, not a requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה only repeats the משנה, or the order might be required.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order is the ideal way, and a reversed order is still valid after the fact.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The order of חליצה is the ideal way but does not hold back its validity.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports that switching the order still works
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the shoe removal came before the spitting, or the spitting came first, the חליצה is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: whether he did the shoe removal before the spitting, or the spitting before the shoe removal, what he did counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports what it just said about רב יהודה: the order is the proper way, but switching it does not ruin the חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said רב יהודה's order is only the proper way to do it. This ברייתא says it openly: either order of חליצה and רקיקה is valid once it has been done. So the earlier answer now has a source behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this. It brings support for what was just said.
The spitting done by the יבמה during חליצה
What he did is done. It counts after the fact.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא:
Whether he did the shoe removal before the spitting,
or he did the spitting before the shoe removal,
what he did is done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 8 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the order of the חליצה actions is only the proper way and does not stop the חליצה from being valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that either order, shoe first or spitting first, is valid after the fact.

steps.title: Read the negative phrases together, not split up
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the one prompting must read 'לא אבה יבמי' and 'לא חפצתי לקחתה' as one phrase, so they do not sound like the opposite meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The one who prompts the reading for חליצה should not prompt her with 'not' by itself and then 'my יבם wishes' by itself, because that sounds like 'my יבם does wish.' Instead he should say 'my יבם did not wish' all together. And he should not prompt the יבם with 'not' by itself and then 'I wish' by itself, because that sounds like 'I wish to take her.' Instead he should say 'I do not wish to take her' all together.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new practical rule about how the prompter reads the פסוקים to the יבמה and the יבם during חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the prompter stops right after the word 'לא', the next words heard alone mean the opposite: 'my יבם wants' or 'I want to take her.' So אביי says each negative sentence must be read in one go, so the meaning stays clear.

keyTerms.meaning: Prompts someone to read, by reading the words first so they can repeat them
Here, the חליצה text that is read aloud
By itself, separately
Because it sounds like / it implies
My יבם did not wish (to do יבום). These are words of the יבמה.
I do not wish to take her. These are words of the יבם.

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not adding words to the פסוק. He is only talking about where the prompter pauses, so that no part of the reading sounds like the opposite meaning.

phrases.english: אביי said:
The one who prompts the reading for the חליצה text
phrases.notes: Literally 'the חליצה document'. Here it means the words the יבמה and יבם read aloud.

phrases.english: should not prompt her with 'not' by itself
and then 'my יבם wishes' by itself,
because it sounds like: 'my יבם does wish.'
Rather, he should say: 'My יבם did not wish' all together.
And he should not prompt him (the יבם) with 'not' by itself
and then 'I wish' by itself,
because it sounds like 'I wish to take her,'
Rather, he should say 'I do not wish to take her' all together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how the חליצה פסוקים must be read aloud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prompter must read 'לא אבה יבמי' and 'לא חפצתי לקחתה' without a break after 'לא'.

steps.title: רבא: a pause in speech is no problem
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי: splitting the phrase is just a pause in speaking, and such a pause does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is just a break in the speech, and a break in the speech does not bother us.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite view to אביי about pausing in the middle of the negative phrases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי worried that the second half, heard alone, means the opposite. רבא says everyone understands it is one sentence with a pause in the middle, so the meaning does not change. In his view the pause is no problem at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A break or pause in the middle of speaking
It does not bother us. It is no problem.

steps.whyThisMatters: The next step is built on רבא's view. רב אשי uses it to question why רב כהנא was working so hard.

phrases.english: רבא said:
It is just a break in the speech,
and a break in the speech does not bother us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's rule in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pausing in the middle of the phrase is only a break in speech and does not harm the חליצה.

steps.title: רב אשי questions רב כהנא's extra effort
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי sees רב כהנא working hard to get a יבמה to say 'לא אבה יבמי' together, and asks whether he does not hold like רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי found רב כהנא working hard while prompting a יבמה to say 'My יבם did not wish.' He said to him: Doesn't the master hold of this teaching of רבא?
steps.whatsHappening: A short story: רב אשי challenges רב כהנא for working so hard to keep the phrase together, since רבא said a pause is no problem. This sets up רב כהנא's answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא is acting like אביי and insisting on no break. רב אשי points out that by רבא's rule all this effort is not needed. So the question is why רב כהנא was so strict.

keyTerms.meaning: He found him
Who was straining, working hard
Doesn't the master hold of...? A polite way of challenging a teacher.

phrases.english: רב אשי found רב כהנא
working hard while prompting her (a יבמה)
phrases.notes: She was having trouble saying it together, so he kept trying to get her to say it in one go.

phrases.english: 'My יבם did not wish,'
He (רב אשי) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא סָבַר לֵיהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרָבָא?
phrases.english: Doesn't the master hold of this teaching of רבא?
phrases.notes: This is רבא's rule from the step before: a pause in speech is no problem.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לֵיהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's rule from step 11 to question רב כהנא's practice, which matches אביי in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's effort to make the יבמה say 'לא אבה יבמי' with no break.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא said a pause in speech does not matter, so all this effort seems to be for nothing.

steps.title: רבא agrees about 'לא אבה יבמי'
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers רב אשי: even רבא agrees that 'לא אבה יבמי' must be said as one phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבא agrees when it comes to 'לא אבה יבמי'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers רב אשי's question. He was not going against רבא, because רבא agrees about this phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא limits רבא's rule: a pause does not matter in the man's line, 'לא חפצתי לקחתה', but for the woman's line 'לא אבה יבמי' even רבא agrees with אביי that the words must stay together. So רב כהנא's effort was not against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: agrees (here: agrees in this one case)
'he did not wish to do יבום with me', the woman's words

steps.confusionAlert: רבא did not change his mind. He still holds that a pause in 'לא חפצתי לקחתה' is fine. He only agrees about the woman's phrase 'לא אבה יבמי'.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב כהנא is answering רב אשי.

phrases.english: Rava agrees
regarding "he did not wish to do yibum with me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of רבא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא holds that a pause never matters, so רב כהנא's effort was unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's ruling covers only the man's phrase. For 'לא אבה יבמי' he agrees with אביי.

steps.title: How to write a שטר חליצה
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives the exact wording for a שטר חליצה, recording which פסוקים each side was told to read.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Someone writing a שטר חליצה should write: We had her read from 'מאן יבמי' until 'אבה יבמי', we had him read from 'לא' until 'לקחתה', and we had her read from 'ככה' until 'חלוץ הנעל'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי teaches the wording of the document the בית דין writes after a חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The document records who read which part. She reads her complaint, from 'מאן יבמי' to 'אבה יבמי'. He reads his refusal, from 'לא' to 'לקחתה'. Then she reads the closing words, from 'ככה' through 'חלוץ הנעל', which matches the custom of finishing the whole פרשה.

keyTerms.meaning: a document recording that חליצה was done
we had her read (we prompted her to say)
'the one whose shoe was removed', the last words of the passage

phrases.english: Abaye said:
One who writes a document of chalitza —
should write like this:
We had her read
from "my brother-in-law refuses" until "wish to do yibum with me,"
and we had him read
from "not" until "to take her,"
phrases.notes: This is his line, 'לא חפצתי לקחתה', in דברים 25:8.

phrases.english: and we had her read
from "so" until "the one whose shoe was removed."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מַאן דְּכָתֵב גִּיטָּא דַּחֲלִיצְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how the words are said to how the event is recorded in writing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטר חליצה records that she read from 'מאן יבמי' to 'אבה יבמי', he read from 'לא' to 'לקחתה', and she read from 'ככה' to 'חלוץ הנעל'.

steps.title: מר זוטרא writes out the whole passage
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא used to rule lines and write the entire תורה passage of חליצה in the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא would rule lines and write the whole passage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what מר זוטרא did. Instead of only naming the start and end words, he wrote out the full פרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ruling lines is how words of the תורה are written properly. So מר זוטרא treated the passage as real פסוקים and wrote all of them out in the document. This sets up the next objection.

keyTerms.meaning: rules guide lines on the parchment
a section of the Torah

phrases.english: Mar Zutra would rule lines
phrases.notes: He drew guide lines on the parchment, the way you do before writing words of the תורה.

phrases.english: and write the whole passage.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא מְשַׂרְטֵט וְכָתֵיב לְכוּלַּהּ פָּרָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different way to write the שטר חליצה than אביי's short version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole חליצה passage may be written out, on ruled lines, in the document.

steps.title: מר בר אידי objects: pieces of the תורה are not written alone
steps.stepSummary: מר בר אידי challenges מר זוטרא: a section of the תורה may not be written on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר אידי objected: But it was not permitted to be written!
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר אידי attacks מר זוטרא's practice of writing out the whole passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Parts of the תורה are not supposed to be written as separate pieces. Writing the full פרשה on its own parchment looks like breaking that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: he strongly challenged it
it was not given to be written (on its own)

phrases.english: Mar bar Idi challenged it:
But it was not given to be written!
phrases.notes: He means a piece of the תורה isn't supposed to be written out by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges מר זוטרא's practice from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's writing of the whole פרשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Torah sections may not be written separately, so writing the whole passage seems forbidden.

steps.title: The הלכה follows מר זוטרא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like מר זוטרא: the passage may be written in the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows מר זוטרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument. We follow מר זוטרא even with מר בר אידי's objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection does not change the ruling. Writing out the whole פרשה in a שטר חליצה is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: the הלכה follows him

steps.whatToRemember: A שטר חליצה may contain the full Torah passage, as מר זוטרא did.

phrases.english: And the halacha follows Mar Zutra.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between מר זוטרא and מר בר אידי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is like מר זוטרא; the whole passage may be written in the שטר חליצה.

steps.title: Spit blown away by the wind
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the spit must reach the area in front of the יבם's face; if wind carries it off before that, the חליצה is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If she spat and the wind caught it, she did nothing. Why? We need 'and she shall spit before him'. So if he is tall and she is short and the wind caught it, it was already 'before him'. If she is tall and he is short, it must reach the level of his face before it blows away.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new topic: the rules of the spitting. He explains exactly when wind ruins it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'בפניו', in front of his face. If he is taller, the spit is level with his face the moment it leaves her mouth, so wind after that doesn't matter. If she is taller, the spit has to drop down to his face level before the wind takes it.

keyTerms.meaning: she spat
the wind caught it
'and she shall spit before him' (the פסוק)
she has done nothing at all; the act does not count
short (man / woman)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If she spat and the wind caught it —
she has done nothing at all.
What is the reason?
We need "and she shall spit before him."
Therefore, if he is tall and she is short,
and the wind caught it —
there is "before him."
If she is tall and he is short —
we need it to reach opposite his face
and only then go off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the details of the spitting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spit must reach the space in front of the יבם's face. Wind that carries it away before then makes the act not count.

steps.title: Spit caused by garlic or clay does not count
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if she ate garlic or clay to make herself spit, the spitting does not count; it must come on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If she ate garlic and spat, or ate clay and spat, she did nothing. Why? We need 'and she shall spit' on her own, and that is missing here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds another spitting rule: the spit has to be her own, not spit caused by something she ate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Garlic or clay fills the mouth with spit. Spitting it out is then caused by the food, not a real act of spitting by her. The פסוק 'וירקה' means she herself spits.

keyTerms.meaning: garlic
a type of clay that was chewed
on her own

phrases.english: Rava said:
If she ate garlic and spat,
if she ate clay and spat —
she has done nothing at all.
What is the reason?
We need "and she shall spit" on her own,
and that is not here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second requirement for valid spitting after אביי's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spitting caused by eating garlic or clay is not valid. The spitting must come from her alone.

steps.title: The judges must see the spit leave her mouth
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the judges must see the spit as it comes out of the יבמה's mouth, based on 'לעיני הזקנים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The judges need to see the spit as it comes out of the יבמה's mouth, as it is written: 'Before the eyes of the elders ... and she shall spit.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third spitting rule: the judges have to watch it happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not enough for the judges to find spit on the ground afterward. The פסוק ties 'לעיני הזקנים' (before the eyes of the elders) to 'וירקה', so the spitting itself must happen in front of them.

keyTerms.meaning: judges
spit
before the eyes of the elders (the בית דין)

steps.whatToRemember: Valid spitting needs three things: it reaches in front of his face (אביי), it is her own natural spit (רבא), and the judges see it leave her mouth (רבא).

phrases.english: And Rava said:
The judges need to see the spit
as it comes out of the yevama's mouth.
As it is written:
"Before the eyes of the elders ... and she shall spit."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: צְרִיכִי דַּיָּינֵי לְמִיחְזֵי רוּקָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further statement of רבא adding another spitting requirement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The judges must see the spit leave the יבמה's mouth, based on the פסוק 'לעיני הזקנים ... וירקה'.

steps.title: Only the judges must call out the closing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: calling out 'בית חלוץ הנעל' is a מצוה for the judges, not for the students.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And his name shall be called in Israel: the house of the one whose shoe was removed.' This is a מצוה for the judges, not for the students.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a line from the משנה about who must call out the words 'חלוץ הנעל' at the end of a חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the man's name 'shall be called' this. The ruling quoted here limits that job to the judges, the people running the חליצה. Students who are just watching do not have to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: And his name shall be called
The house of the one whose shoe was removed
Judges
Students, the people watching

phrases.english: "And his name shall be called in Israel:
The house of the one whose shoe was removed" —
it is a מצוה for the judges, and not for the students.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בֵּית חֲלוּץ הַנָּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the rules about spitting to the last part of the חליצה ceremony, calling out the words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Calling out 'חלוץ הנעל' is a מצוה for the judges, not the students.

steps.title: רבי טרפון had everyone call out the words
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יהודה tells how רבי טרפון told all the students present to call out 'חלוץ הנעל' three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה said: Once we were sitting before רבי טרפון, and a יבמה came to do חליצה. He said to us: All of you answer, 'חלוץ הנעל, חלוץ הנעל, חלוץ הנעל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story from a ברייתא where רבי טרפון had all the students call out the words, not just the judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step before limited the מצוה to the judges. Here רבי טרפון told everyone sitting there, the students too, to answer. This story backs up רבי יהודה's view, which is that everyone standing there joins in. The words were said three times.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A תנא; רבי יהודה sat before him
All of you answer
The widow who needs יבום or חליצה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the step before. That ruling limited the מצוה to the judges, but this story shows students joining in. This fits the view of רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: It was taught: רבי יהודה said:
Once we were sitting
before רבי טרפון,
and a יבמה came to do חליצה,
and he said to us: All of you answer:
"The one whose shoe was removed," "The one whose shoe was removed," "The one whose shoe was removed."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: פַּעַם אַחַת הָיִינוּ יוֹשְׁבִים לִפְנֵי רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practice where everyone present calls out the words, unlike the judges-only line in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that everyone present calls out 'חלוץ הנעל'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא telling what רבי טרפון did at a חליצה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views. One says only the judges call out 'חלוץ הנעל'. The other is רבי יהודה's view, backed by רבי טרפון's practice, that everyone present calls it out three times.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing מצות חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The closing words for the chapter מצות חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter מצות חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line that marks the end of the chapter מצות חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks that the chapter is finished and shows a hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you
The name of this chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you,
מצות חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the last ruling about the חליצה ceremony.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter מצות חליצה is finished.
